findings.message: The postCreateCommand installs `.[dev]`, but the project has no `dev` extra, so the container never gets pytest, pytest-asyncio, mypy or types-requests, even though the README says it installs all dependencies. pyproject.toml uses `build-backend = "hatchling.build"` and declares only `[project] dependencies`, with no `[project.optional-dependencies]`. The `dev` extra exists only in setup.py `extras_require`, and hatchling ignores setup.py. `uv pip install -e '.[dev]'` therefore installs the runtime dependencies and drops the missing extra (uv only warns). The dev tools are listed in requirements-dev.in, which nothing in the devcontainer installs.

The container omits development dependencies, so developers cannot run the repository's tests after setup. On a fresh container, postCreateCommand installs only '.[dev]', but pyproject.toml defines no dev optional dependency group. pytest and pytest-asyncio are declared separately in requirements-dev.in, which this command never installs; the tests import pytest and use its asyncio plugin.

`workspaceFolder` is hard-coded to /workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus without a matching `workspaceMount`, so a clone in a folder with any other name opens in a directory that doesn't exist, and the postCreateCommand and the interpreter path both fail. devcontainer.json sets `"workspaceFolder": "/workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus"` and `"python.defaultInterpreterPath": "/workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus/.venv/bin/python"` but has no `workspaceMount`. The default mount target is /workspaces/${localWorkspaceFolderBasename}, so a clone named e.g. `proxmox-mcp-plus` or `ProxmoxMCP-Plus-main` is mounted somewhere else. `${containerWorkspaceFolder}` and `${localWorkspaceFolderBasename}` were not used.

Opening a checkout with a different directory name selects a nonexistent workspace and breaks dependency installation. workspaceFolder is fixed to /workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus without a corresponding workspaceMount. The default local workspace mount follows the checkout directory name, so a checkout named proxmox mounts elsewhere while postCreateCommand targets the fixed workspace. The interpreter path on line 20 repeats the same assumption.

The README says the OpenAPI proxy is reachable at http://localhost:8811 once port 8811 is forwarded, but nothing in the dev container starts the proxy, so users following the steps will find nothing on that port. devcontainer.json has only `postCreateCommand` (venv plus install), with no `postStartCommand` and no run of start_openapi.sh. The README steps never tell the user to run `./start_openapi.sh` or `python -m proxmox_mcp.openapi_proxy`. Step 4 reads: "Port `8811` is forwarded automatically so the OpenAPI proxy is reachable at `http://localhost:8811`."

The dev image pulls an unpinned base image and an unpinned `uv` from PyPI, so builds aren't reproducible and the supply-chain input can change without anyone noticing. `FROM python:3.11-slim` has no digest, and `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv` has no version pin. The `uv pip install -e` that follows resolves the open-ended `>=` ranges in pyproject.toml, and no lockfile is used (`.gitignore` excludes `uv.lock`).

`build-essential` is added to the dev image although no dependency is shown to need a compiler, which makes the image bigger and gives it more attack surface than the existing Dockerfile has. The root Dockerfile installs only `git curl` and builds the same dependency set. The new .devcontainer/Dockerfile adds `build-essential`, and the change gives no reason for it.

The README claims the container installs "all Python dependencies" and comes with Ruff and Black, but the Python dev toolchain (pytest/mypy) is missing, and Ruff/Black are only present through the VS Code extensions' bundled binaries, so the documentation overstates what the environment gives you. README step 2: "installs all Python dependencies automatically (`uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`)". As shown above, `.[dev]` resolves to no extra under hatchling. The only thing in devcontainer.json that provides ruff and black is the `extensions` list (`charliermarsh.ruff`, `ms-python.black-formatter`).
